primary_source.citation: Yi Yu, Tengyao Wang and Richard J. Samworth, A useful variant of the Davis--Kahan theorem for statisticians, Biometrika 102(2), 2015, 315--323; preprint arXiv:1405.0680.
primary_source.private_comparison_source: A local transcription of the 2014 preprint (SHA-256 ed45f19e...) was used to build prose/distilled_literature/YuWangSamworth2015_statistical_davis_kahan.tex. It is deliberately not distributed, so no row may be resolved by consulting it here.
primary_source.numbering_convention: This census keys on the PUBLISHED Biometrika numbering, checked against the article on 2026-08-13: Theorem 1 (the Davis--Kahan baseline), Theorem 2 (the population-gap theorem), Corollary 1 (the single-eigenvector case), Theorem 3 (singular subspaces), Lemma A1 (the appendix compression lemma), displayed equations (1)-(4), and appendix equations (A1)-(A8). The 2014 arXiv preprint shares one counter across environments and therefore numbers the same results Theorem 1, Theorem 2, Corollary 3, Theorem 4, Lemma 5; many Lean declaration names used by the `YuWangSamworth2015` package still carry that preprint numbering. The correspondence is Corollary 1 = Corollary 3, Theorem 3 = Theorem 4, Lemma A1 = Lemma 5. See gap `preprint-numbering-aliases`.
primary_source.published_source_audit: The published article was read on 2026-08-13 and differs from the 2014 preprint in three ways this census records. (a) Numbering, as above. (b) Theorem 1's mixed separation is printed as `delta = inf{|lambda-hat - lambda| : lambda in [lambda_s, lambda_r], lambda-hat in (-inf, lambda-hat_{s+1}] u [lambda-hat_{r-1}, inf)}` with `lambda-hat_0 = -inf`, `lambda-hat_{p+1} = inf`; the preprint prints `lambda-hat_{s-1}` and `lambda-hat_{r+1}`, which are the wrong endpoints for a decreasing spectrum. The published indices are correct and are what `prose/distilled_literature/YuWangSamworth2015_statistical_davis_kahan.tex` now records. The published VALUES assigned to `lambda-hat_0` and `lambda-hat_{p+1}` are nevertheless inverted, which makes Theorem 1 vacuous at any block touching an end of the spectrum; see gap `theorem1-sample-endpoint-conventions`, added 2026-08-29. (c) The Section 2 orthogonal-blocks sharpness example is a MIDDLE block in the published article (`Sigma = diag(5,...,5,3,...,3,1,...,1)` and `Sigma-hat` with first `p-2d` entries 5, next `d` entries 2, last `d` entries `2+eps`), whereas the preprint uses a top block (`Sigma = diag(3,...,3,1,...,1)`, `Sigma-hat = diag(2-eps,...,2-eps,2,...,2)`). Both constructions were formalized by 2026-08-13, the published one in `YuWangSamworth2015/YuWangSamworth2015/Symmetric/MiddleBlockSharpness.lean`; the gap that recorded the difference is retired. (d) The published article also carries a Section 1 numerical illustration, `Sigma = diag(50,40,30,20,10)` and `Sigma-hat = diag(54,37,32,23,21)`, showing that Theorem 1's separation can vanish; it is row `YWS-S1-toy-example` and is formalized.

how_to_use:
Two independent axes. `status` is the mathematical judgement against the printed source; `verification` is what the Lean build certifies and is measured, not asserted -- run with `--probe` to resolve every declaration against the real build targets. To find the frontier, filter on `verification`: `absent` rows need new work, `proved_outside_build` rows are already proved and only need wiring into a default target, and `gap_refs` names the specific obstruction in `gaps`. `lean_declarations` names declarations that exist; `planned_declarations` names ones this census wants and nobody has written. Every result in the paper has a row whether or not anything formalizes it -- that is the point of keying on the source rather than on the Lean tree.

The `importance` field is an external-review priority. `headline` selects the paper's central auditable theorem surface; `major` additionally includes the baseline, rank-one corollary, and singular-subspace extension.

status_definitions.compiled_exact: A source-facing theorem matching the printed statement is compiled.
status_definitions.compiled_generalized: The result is compiled in a form strictly stronger or more general than printed (for example any unitarily invariant norm in place of Frobenius, or an intrinsic subspace in place of a matrix of columns).
status_definitions.compiled_specialization: A useful compiled specialization exists, but not the full printed scope.
status_definitions.compiled_corrected: The printed statement is false as transcribed; a corrected statement is compiled, together with a machine-checked refutation of the printed one.
status_definitions.not_represented: No matching declaration was found anywhere in the repository.
status_definitions.not_proof_debt: Exposition, literature comparison, or a definition absorbed into a different formulation. Should be documented but is not formalization debt and must not be counted as a gap.

verification_definitions.proved_in_build: Every declaration resolves against a default build target -- `DavisKahan.All` or `YuWangSamworth2015`, which joined `defaultTargets` on 2026-08-02. The default build carries no sorry, so this is a proof continuously re-checked by CI.
verification_definitions.proved_outside_build: Every declaration resolves, but only against a library outside `defaultTargets`, so the mathematics is done and nothing would notice if it broke. NO ROW IS IN THIS STATE: `YuWangSamworth2015` was the only such library for this paper and it is now a default target. Kept as a definition so that a future row landing here is read correctly rather than looking like a new category.
verification_definitions.partially_in_build: Some declarations resolve against a default target and some do not, so the row's source claim is only partly guarded by CI.
verification_definitions.not_applicable: An exposition or literature-comparison item. No formalization is intended, so the row is not proof debt and must not be counted as a gap.

not-proof-debt.title: Exposition and literature comparison
not-proof-debt.detail: Section 3's audit of statistical applications makes claims about other authors' proof patterns, not new perturbation theorems, and the appendix's self-adjoint dilation route is an alternative proof rather than a source obligation. Neither is a formalization gap. Since 2026-08-13 the deterministic mathematical content of the Section 3 diagnosis is nevertheless compiled -- see row `YWS-S3-applications` -- so the row's `verification` is now `proved_in_build`; that does not make it proof debt, and it must still not be counted as a gap.

private-helper-only.title: Some source content exists only as a `private` helper
private-helper-only.detail: Three declarations this census initially cited turned out to be `private`: `sinThetaFrobenius_eq_sqrt_sum_cross` (YuWangSamworth2015/YuWangSamworth2015/Core/Statistics.lean), `yuWangSamworth_gram_alignedBasis_le` and `rectangularFrobenius_comp_adjoint_linearIsometry` (YuWangSamworth2015). They compile and are correct, and they cannot be cited from outside their module. **A `#check` cannot tell a private declaration from a deleted one** -- both fail identically -- which is why the probe now reports the two cases separately; conflating them would let a census report proved mathematics as absent, or absent mathematics as proved. For two of the three the row has a public sibling and nothing is lost. `YWS-S1-complement-identity` had no public sibling -- the identity `‖V_1^T V-hat‖_F = ‖sin Theta‖_F` was proved and unciteable -- and was **fixed on 2026-07-29** by making that one declaration public. The remaining two are genuine internal factoring steps and should stay private.

preprint-numbering-aliases.title: Lean declaration names still carry the preprint numbering
preprint-numbering-aliases.detail: RESOLVED as a source question on 2026-08-13 by reading the published Biometrika article: the numbering is Theorem 1, Theorem 2, Corollary 1, Theorem 3, Lemma A1, and this census and `prose/distilled_literature/YuWangSamworth2015_statistical_davis_kahan.tex` now use it. What remains is cosmetic and deliberate: declarations used by `YuWangSamworth2015`, such as `yuWangSamworth_theorem1_uiNorm_le` and `yuWangSamworth_lemma5_columns`, still spell the preprint's flat numbering, and `comparator/*.json` pins some of those strings. Renaming them would break pinned comparator configurations for no mathematical gain, so the translation table lives here instead: Corollary 1 = Corollary 3, Theorem 3 = Theorem 4, Lemma A1 = Lemma 5. A row's `source_anchor` is always the published name.

theorem3-rank-boundary.title: The printed rank-boundary convention of Theorem 3 is false
theorem3-rank-boundary.detail: Published Theorem 3 fixes `1 <= r <= s <= rank(A)` and defines `sigma_0^2 = inf` and `sigma_{rank(A)+1}^2 = -inf`. The second convention is wrong. The paper's own proof passes to `A^T A in R^{q x q}` -- 'with eigenvalues sigma_1^2 >= ... >= sigma_q^2' -- and applies Theorem 2, whose convention is `lambda_{q+1} = -inf`, at the AMBIENT index `q`. When `rank(A) < q` the Gram operator still has a zero eigenspace and the two conventions disagree there. Taking `s = rank(A)` then makes the printed denominator infinite, so the printed bound asserts `||sin Theta||_F <= 0` while the two right singular subspaces can be orthogonal. Machine-checked refutation: `YuWangSamworth2015.DavisKahanTheory.yuWangSamworth_theorem3_printed_rankBoundary_refutation` and its `ℝ^2` instance. The repair -- read the convention at the ambient dimension, with `sigma_j = 0` for `min(p,q) < j` -- is what the repository proves, because its gap hypothesis is the intrinsic separation of the sorted spectrum of `A*A`. Found 2026-08-13; no erratum is known.

literal-index-wrappers.title: Equation (1) has no wrapper with a literal index j and a mixed gap
literal-index-wrappers.detail:
NARROWED 2026-08-13. This gap used to cover every source statement: the theorems took an index embedding `e : Fin d -> Fin n` and an intrinsic separation, and none took the paper's literal contiguous range `r <= j <= s` with the gap read off as `min(lambda_{r-1} - lambda_r, lambda_s - lambda_{s+1})`. That is now delivered for the POPULATION-gap results by `YuWangSamworth2015.consecutiveEmb` and `YuWangSamworth2015.OrderedBlockBoundaryGap` -- Theorem 2's two conclusions and both residual forms (`yuWangSamworth_sinTheta_block_le` and siblings), Corollary 1 (`yuWangSamworth_corollary1_sinTheta_le`, `..._real_le`), and Theorem 3 on both sides in singular-value notation (`yuWangSamworth_rightSingularSubspace_block_le` and siblings).

What remains is equation (1), the `r = s = j` specialization of THEOREM 1, whose denominator is the MIXED separation `min(|lambda-hat_{j-1} - lambda_j|, |lambda-hat_{j+1} - lambda_j|)`. The boundary-gap machinery above does not apply to it: it converts a boundary condition on one sorted spectrum into an intrinsic separation of that same spectrum, whereas equation (1) compares the population eigenvalue against the SAMPLE spectrum. A literal index wrapper for it would also need the sample eigenline to be determined -- with `lambda-hat_j` repeated, `V-perp` carries `lambda-hat_j` itself and the mixed exterior gap is zero -- so it needs a simplicity hypothesis the source does not print at that display. Since Theorem 1 is already proved here in a strictly more general unitarily invariant interval form, this is source recognizability for a baseline result the paper itself is arguing against, not a mathematical gap.

theorem1-sample-endpoint-conventions.title: Theorem 1's printed sample endpoint conventions make it vacuous at end blocks
theorem1-sample-endpoint-conventions.detail: Published Theorem 1 defines `delta = inf{|lambda-hat - lambda| : lambda in [lambda_s, lambda_r], lambda-hat in (-inf, lambda-hat_{s+1}] u [lambda-hat_{r-1}, inf)}` with `lambda-hat_0 = -inf` and `lambda-hat_{p+1} = inf`. Those two values are inverted relative to what the definition needs. At `r = 1` the ray `[lambda-hat_0, inf)` is the whole line, at `s = p` the ray `(-inf, lambda-hat_{p+1}]` is the whole line, and in either case the infimum is 0, so the hypothesis `delta > 0` is unsatisfiable and Theorem 1 has no content at any block touching an end of the spectrum -- including the top-`d` block, the common case in statistics. The reading the theorem evidently intends is `lambda-hat_0 = +inf` and `lambda-hat_{p+1} = -inf`, which make the missing ray EMPTY, exactly as Theorem 2's `lambda_0 = +inf`, `lambda_{p+1} = -inf` do for the population gaps. Confirmed against the published Biometrika article on 2026-08-29; this file's `published_source_audit` clause (b) had recorded the conventions correctly but had not observed the consequence. Milder in kind than the other printed defects: it degrades a baseline theorem to vacuity rather than asserting something false, and Theorem 1 is the result the paper argues against rather than a contribution of it. The Lean development is unaffected either way -- `yuWangSamworth_theorem1_uiNorm_le` phrases the separation as `IntervalExteriorGap`, an intrinsic spectral condition, and never used the printed conventions. What it blocks is the claim that a paper-facing statement IS the printed `delta`; see `registry/YWS_SOURCE_CONTRACT.md` in the Yu--Wang--Samworth submission repository `AIQ-Kitware/aiq-yu-wang-samworth-2015-useful-variant-davis-kahan-statisticians-formalization` row T1. No erratum is known.

corollary1-printed-normalization.title: The standalone printed Corollary 1 omits the normalization its own d = 1 reading supplies
corollary1-printed-normalization.detail: Published Corollary 1 says only: 'If v, v-hat in R^p satisfy Sigma v = lambda_j v and SigmaHat v-hat = lambdaHat_j v-hat, then ...'. It does not say the two vectors are unit. Unit vectors are unambiguously what is meant -- the sentence introducing the corollary presents it as the `d = 1` case of Theorem 2 ('Many if not most applications of this result will need only s = r, i.e., d = 1. In that case, the statement simplifies a little; for ease of reference, we state it as a corollary'), and Theorem 2's V and V-hat have orthonormal columns. The omission is nevertheless not harmless. The eigenvector equations are homogeneous and the orientation condition v-hat^T v >= 0 only becomes more true under scaling, so from any instance take SigmaHat := Sigma and v-hat := 2v: every printed hypothesis holds, the perturbation is zero, the printed bound is 0, and ||v-hat - v|| = ||v||. The SECOND printed display is therefore false as literally stated. Machine-checked refutation: `YuWangSamworth2015.corollary1_printed_unnormalized_counterexample`. The printed first display survives scaling, being about the angle between two spans, though it is degenerate at v-hat = 0, which the printed hypotheses also admit. The Lean statements have always assumed ||v|| = ||v-hat|| = 1; what changed on 2026-08-29 is that this is now recorded as a source divergence rather than described as 'exactly the printed statement'. The Palomar symmetric entry keeps `relationship: formalizes`, because the hypothesis written out is the source's own from one sentence earlier, but it no longer claims 'no added hypothesis'. No erratum is known.

items.title: Principal angles, sin-Theta, and the Frobenius sine identity
items.summary: For V, V-hat with orthonormal columns the principal angles are the arccosines of the singular values of V-hat^T V, and the Frobenius sine distance satisfies ‖sin Theta‖_F^2 = d - ‖V-hat^T V‖_F^2.
items.notes: The Lean development defines the sine distance intrinsically on subspaces rather than on a matrix of chosen columns, and then proves it agrees with the span-based form. That is why no basis is a hypothesis anywhere downstream. The bridge lemma `sinThetaFrobenius_eq_sqrt_sum_cross` was `private` until 2026-07-29 and is now public.

items.title: ‖V_1^T V-hat‖_F = ‖sin Theta(V-hat, V)‖_F
items.summary: The cross-block energy against an orthonormal complement of V equals the Frobenius sine distance.
items.notes: Closed 2026-07-29. The identity was proved all along but the declaration was `private`, so nothing outside its module could cite it and this row correctly read `absent` -- the one item in this census where the mathematics existed and the API did not. It is now public, with a docstring saying why. **The census is what found it**: a coverage claim assembled from the Lean side would have counted the proof and never noticed that no reader could reach it.

items.title: Procrustes alignment: ‖V-hat O - V‖_F <= sqrt 2 ‖sin Theta‖_F
items.summary: Minimizing over orthogonal O gives ‖V-hat O - V‖_F^2 = 2 sum (1 - cos theta_j) <= 2 sum sin^2 theta_j.
items.notes:
The sqrt-2 step is the whole reason the aligned-basis constant is 2^{3/2} rather than 2. It lives in ForTauCeti as a reusable orthonormal-family result, not as a matrix Procrustes computation.

Extended 2026-08-13. `exists_aligned_orthonormalBasis` gives the numerical step but hides the alignment: it replaces BOTH frames by unnamed frames of the same spans, so a reader cannot see that the population frame is untouched and cannot recover `O-hat`. `frameComp hv O` is the paper's matrix product `V-hat O-hat` -- column `i` is `sum_j O_{ji} v-hat_j` -- and `exists_unitary_sum_sq_norm_frameComp_sub_le` states the Procrustes step with the alignment exhibited and the population frame fixed. `O-hat` is a bundled linear isometry equivalence of the block's coordinate space, which over R is exactly an element of O(d); `adjoint_comp_self_eq_id` spells that out as `O-hat^T O-hat = I`. Over `R` the alignment is produced as an honest matrix: `frameAlignMatrix O` is the `d x d` matrix `O_{ji} = (O e_i)_j` and `frameAlignMatrix_mem_orthogonalGroup` places it in `Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) R`, so `O-hat in O(d)` needs no interpretation.

items.title: Theorem 1 -- the statistical Davis--Kahan baseline (mixed gap)
items.summary: With a mixed spectral separation delta > 0 between the perturbed and population blocks, ‖sin Theta(V-hat, V)‖_F <= ‖Sigma-hat - Sigma‖_F / delta; the paper notes both norms may be replaced by the operator norm or any orthogonally invariant norm.
items.notes:
The paper's 'any orthogonally invariant norm' remark is the primary Lean statement, not an afterthought: `yuWangSamworth_theorem1_uiNorm_le` takes a `UnitarilyInvariantSeminorm` and the Frobenius and operator forms are its specializations. So the strongest advertised form is the one that is proved.

Source note added 2026-08-13. The published article prints the mixed separation as `delta = inf{|lambda-hat - lambda| : lambda in [lambda_s, lambda_r], lambda-hat in (-inf, lambda-hat_{s+1}] u [lambda-hat_{r-1}, inf)}`. The 2014 preprint prints `lambda-hat_{s-1}` and `lambda-hat_{r+1}` instead, which name the wrong endpoints for a decreasing spectrum; the published indices are the correct ones. The distilled TeX carried the preprint's indices (with a comment calling them awkward) and now carries the published ones. The Lean statements are phrased with intrinsic spectral-separation predicates and were never affected either way.

**Printed endpoint conventions, 2026-08-29.** A direct read of the published Biometrika article for the Palomar preparation pass confirmed that it prints `lambda-hat_0 = -inf` and `lambda-hat_{p+1} = inf`, and observed the consequence this census had not: those values are inverted for the rays the definition uses, so `delta = 0` and the hypothesis `delta > 0` is unsatisfiable at any block with `r = 1` or `s = p`. See gap `theorem1-sample-endpoint-conventions`. The Lean statements are unaffected -- they phrase the separation as `IntervalExteriorGap`, an intrinsic condition -- but a paper-facing wrapper claiming to state the printed `delta` would have to disclose the correction, which is why Theorem 1 is not selected for a Palomar entry.

semantic_review.claim: With a mixed spectral separation delta > 0 between the perturbed and population blocks, ‖sin Theta(V-hat, V)‖_F <= ‖Sigma-hat - Sigma‖_F / delta; the paper notes both norms may be replaced by the operator norm or any orthogonally invariant norm.

items.title: Equation (1) -- the eigenvector specialization of the baseline
items.summary: For r = s = j the baseline specializes to a single-eigenvector sine bound with a mixed gap, and after choosing the sign so v-hat^T v >= 0, ‖v-hat - v‖ <= sqrt 2 sin theta.
items.notes: Equation (1) is the `r = s = j` specialization of the baseline, followed by the remark that reversing the sign of `v-hat_j` gives `||v-hat_j - v_j|| <= sqrt 2 sin Theta`. The sign-choice half is available as the rank-one case of the aligned-basis machinery; the census does not claim a source-shaped wrapper for equation (1) itself.
items.next_action: Optional: state equation (1) with a literal index j and a mixed gap, for source recognizability. It needs a simplicity hypothesis on lambda-hat_j that the source does not print at that display; see gap literal-index-wrappers.

items.source_anchor: Section 1, numerical illustration that delta can vanish
items.title: Section 1 -- the five-by-five illustration that Theorem 1's separation can vanish
items.summary: Sigma = diag(50,40,30,20,10) and Sigma-hat = diag(54,37,32,23,21): the population eigenvalues are well separated, yet Theorem 1's mixed separation delta is zero for the block of interest, which is the motivation for Theorem 2.
items.notes:
Inventoried on 2026-08-13 after reading the published article, where it appears immediately after Theorem 1; formalized on 2026-08-13 in `YuWangSamworth2015/YuWangSamworth2015/Symmetric/MixedGap.lean`.

Theorem 1's separation is defined over the two RAYS `(-inf, lambda-hat_{s+1}]` and `[lambda-hat_{r-1}, inf)`, not over the sample eigenvalues themselves, and `mixedSeparation` records exactly that: `sInf {|lambda-hat - lambda| : lambda in [a,b], lambda-hat in Iic lo u Ici hi}`. The article selects the eigenvectors for the second, third and fourth largest eigenvalues, so its block is `r = 2`, `s = 4` (zero-based Lean indices 1..3). The block interval is `[lambda_4, lambda_2] = [20, 40]` and the lower exterior ray is `(-inf, lambda-hat_5] = (-inf, 21]`; they meet, so the infimum is attained at zero and Theorem 1 has no content -- `section1_mixedSeparation_eq_zero`. The population gap at the same block is `min(lambda_1 - lambda_2, lambda_4 - lambda_5) = min(50-40, 20-10) = 10`, both numerically (`section1_populationGap`) and at the operator level (`internalGap_section1_paperBlock`, an `InternalGap` for the diagonal model, so the population-gap theorems genuinely apply to this pair; `internalGap_section1` is the same fact at the singleton block `r = s = 4`). `opNorm_section1_perturbation` records `||E||_op = 11`, which is what row `YWS-S3-applications` uses to show the literature's Weyl-recovery step fails here.

The illustration is motivation rather than a step in any proof, and nothing downstream depends on it; it is formalized because a census that leaves a checkable printed assertion unformalized is recording a smaller claim than it appears to.

items.title: Theorem 2, first conclusion -- the population-gap sine bound
items.summary: With only the two exterior POPULATION gaps Delta = min(lambda_{r-1} - lambda_r, lambda_s - lambda_{s+1}) > 0, ‖sin Theta(V-hat, V)‖_F <= 2 min(sqrt d ‖E‖_op, ‖E‖_F) / Delta.
items.notes:
`||sin Theta(V-hat, V)||_F <= 2 min(d^{1/2} ||E||_op, ||E||_F) / Delta` with only the two exterior POPULATION gaps in the denominator. The min is proved as printed, not as one branch.

**Corrected 2026-08-13, and this was a real scope defect.** Until that date the only statement carrying this row was `yuWangSamworth_sinTheta_le`, whose hypothesis `CorrespondingEigenblock hA hB U V` requires BOTH blocks to be spans of the same index set in Mathlib's chosen eigenbases. Yu, Wang and Samworth require only that `V-hat` have orthonormal columns with `Sigma-hat v-hat_j = lambda-hat_j v-hat_j`, and they impose NO sample eigengap -- removing it is the paper's entire contribution. At a repeated sample eigenvalue the two hypotheses differ: the paper admits every orthonormal choice inside the degenerate sample eigenspace, `CorrespondingEigenblock` admits only the one Mathlib happened to pick. Marking the row `compiled_exact` in that state was wrong.

The printed statement is now `yuWangSamworth_sinTheta_frame_le`, whose hypothesis is an arbitrary `IsOrderedEigenframe` on each side at a common index embedding. `yuWangSamworth_sinTheta_le` is derived from it and kept for callers who already hold the index datum. `IsOrderedEigenframe.span_eq_spanIndices` records the asymmetry that makes this correct rather than merely more general: under the population gap the POPULATION block is forced to be the canonical one whatever eigenvectors are chosen, and without a gap -- the sample side -- it is not.

**Indexing closed 2026-08-13.** Until then the only source-general statement was `yuWangSamworth_sinTheta_frame_le`, whose block is an arbitrary index embedding `e : Fin d -> Fin n` and whose gap hypothesis is the intrinsic separation `Delta <= |lambda_{e i} - lambda_k|` for every unselected `k`. That is the right hypothesis for a general theorem but it is not the printed one: the source fixes `1 <= r <= s <= p`, `d = s - r + 1`, and assumes only the two BOUNDARY gaps `min(lambda_{r-1} - lambda_r, lambda_s - lambda_{s+1})`, under the conventions `lambda_0 = +inf` and `lambda_{p+1} = -inf`. `consecutiveEmb` is that block and `OrderedBlockBoundaryGap` is that hypothesis, with the endpoint conventions modelled by VACUOUS QUANTIFICATION (there is no index `q` with `q + 1 = r` when `r = 0`) rather than by extended reals, so the interior, top and bottom blocks need no separate statements. `OrderedBlockBoundaryGap.indexGap` is the bridge, and antitonicity of the sorted spectrum is the only mathematics in it. `yuWangSamworth_sinTheta_block_le` is the printed theorem. The bridge constrains only the POPULATION spectrum, so `lambda-hat_s = lambda-hat_{s+1}` remains admissible -- the wrapper does not smuggle a sample eigengap back in.

The wrappers take the source's own variables `r` and `s`, with the frame size tied to them by `r + d = s + 1` -- the paper's `d = s - r + 1` written without truncated subtraction. `d` cannot be eliminated, since it is the index type of the frames `V, V-hat : Fin d -> E`, but it is pinned by that hypothesis and both the gap and the bound are written at `r` and `s`. The paper's `r <= s` is exactly `1 <= d` here and is not imposed: at `d = 0` the frames are empty and the bound is trivial.

**Paper-facing semantic surface added 2026-08-17.** `theorem2_sinTheta` is now the canonical review declaration. It specializes to real operators on `Real^p`, uses the source names `Sigma`, `SigmaHat`, `V`, `Vhat`, and `Delta`, and states the block arithmetic visibly as `r <= s`, `s < p`, `d = s - r + 1`. `IsEigenvectorBlock` expands directly to orthonormality plus the ordered eigenvalue equations, while `PopulationBoundaryGap` expands directly to the two population boundary inequalities with endpoint vacuity. The previous `yuWangSamworth_sinTheta_block_le` remains the more general implementation-oriented `RCLike` wrapper.

**Exact denominator surface tightened 2026-08-17.** The canonical theorem now assumes `SourcePopulationGap Sigma hSigma r s Delta`, not merely that `Delta` is some lower bound. Outside the full-space endpoint case, `SourcePopulationGap` says that `Delta` is the greatest real satisfying `PopulationBoundaryGap`, hence exactly the printed `min(lambda_{r-1}-lambda_r, lambda_s-lambda_{s+1})` with a missing endpoint omitted. The explicit full-space branch represents the source convention that both exterior gaps are `+inf`; because the theorem is then available for every positive real `Delta`, it captures the infinite-gap limiting case without introducing extended-real arithmetic. `SourcePopulationGap.toPopulationBoundaryGap` forgets exactness and feeds the unchanged implementation theorem. The semantic dictionary also includes `TauCeti.singularValues_sinThetaMap`, closing the displayed `sinThetaFrobenius` quantity to the principal-sine sequence used to define principal angles.

**Readable/auditable norm surface tightened 2026-08-17.** `theorem2_sinTheta` names `sinThetaNorm` explicitly and identifies it by a literal equality hypothesis with the intrinsic Frobenius sine distance. The perturbation term is now written directly as `frobeniusNorm (SigmaHat - Sigma)`, where `frobeniusNorm` is a reducible application-level abbreviation for the existing Frobenius seminorm. Thus the proposition after the colon is closer to the source notation without introducing an opaque scalar parameter.

semantic_review.claim: Theorem 2, first conclusion: the population two-sided exterior gap alone controls the Frobenius sine distance by 2 min(sqrt(d)||E||op,||E||F)/Delta, with no sample eigengap.

setup: Sigma and Sigma-hat are real symmetric p x p matrices with ordered eigenvalues lambda_1>=...>=lambda_p and corresponding d-column eigenvector blocks V and V-hat at indices r,...,s; d=s-r+1; E=Sigma-hat-Sigma.
hypotheses: Delta = min(lambda_{r-1}-lambda_r, lambda_s-lambda_{s+1}) > 0, with lambda_0=+infinity and lambda_{p+1}=-infinity.
No sample-eigenvalue separation hypothesis is assumed.
scope: The canonical Lean declaration is specialized to Real^p to mirror the real symmetric matrix statement; the supporting implementation theorem is RCLike-generic.

context_declarations.name: YuWangSamworth2015.isEigenvectorBlock_iff
context_declarations.mathematical_role: Expands IsEigenvectorBlock completely: orthonormal columns and the ordered eigenvector equation at index r+i. This leaves the sample eigenvectors arbitrary inside repeated eigenspaces.

context_declarations.name: YuWangSamworth2015.sourcePopulationGap_iff

items.title: Theorem 2, second conclusion -- existence of an aligned orthogonal frame
items.summary: There exists O-hat in O(d) with ‖V-hat O-hat - V‖_F <= 2^{3/2} min(sqrt d ‖E‖_op, ‖E‖_F) / Delta.
items.notes:
Stated as the existence of two orthonormal frames spanning the two blocks with the bound on the sum of squared differences, which is the basis-free content of 'there exists an orthogonal alignment `O-hat`'. Constant `2 * sqrt 2 = 2^{3/2}` as printed.

Corrected 2026-08-13 with `YWS-T2-sinTheta`: the same `CorrespondingEigenblock` scope restriction applied here, and `yuWangSamworth_alignedBasis_frame_le` is the printed statement.

**Alignment exposed 2026-08-13.** The earlier statements conclude that there EXIST orthonormal frames of the two blocks with the bound on the sum of squared differences. That is the basis-free content of the printed conclusion and it does prove the numerical claim, but it is weaker in shape than what the paper says: the paper rotates `V-hat` by an orthogonal `O-hat` and compares against `V` itself. `yuWangSamworth_alignedFrame_le` and its consecutive-index form `yuWangSamworth_alignedFrame_block_le` now conclude exactly that -- an explicit orthogonal `O-hat` on the block's coordinate space, the supplied population frame, and `||V-hat O-hat - V||_F <= 2^{3/2} min(...) / Delta`. The row is `compiled_exact` for that reason now, not for the constant alone.

`yuWangSamworth_alignedFrame_block_real_le` is the fully literal form: real symmetric operators, the block `r..s`, the printed boundary gap, and `O-hat` an element of `Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) R` whose columns give `(V-hat O-hat)_i = sum_j O-hat_{ji} v-hat_j`. Every symbol of the printed second conclusion appears in it; the `RCLike` forms are its generalizations.

**Paper-facing semantic surface added 2026-08-17.** `theorem2_alignedFrame` is now the canonical review declaration and shares exactly the same source-shaped hypotheses as `theorem2_sinTheta`. Its conclusion returns `O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) Real` in the orthogonal group and compares the supplied `Vhat O` directly to the supplied `V`. The previous real and `RCLike` block wrappers remain supporting implementation declarations.

**Exact denominator surface tightened 2026-08-17.** The aligned paper-facing wrapper now shares the exact `SourcePopulationGap` hypothesis with the sine conclusion. Thus `Delta` is the printed population minimum rather than an arbitrary positive lower bound; only the bridge to the existing implementation theorem forgets that exactness.

**Readable/auditable norm surface tightened 2026-08-17.** `theorem2_alignedFrame` writes the perturbation term directly as `frobeniusNorm (SigmaHat - Sigma)`, using the same reducible application-level abbreviation as the first conclusion. The aligned left-hand side remains fully explicit, so no geometry is hidden from the displayed claim.

items.title: Sharpness example: orthogonal blocks, in both the preprint and published forms
items.summary: Preprint form: `Sigma = diag(3,...,3,1,...,1)` and `Sigma-hat = diag(2-eps,...,2-eps,2,...,2)` have orthogonal top-d eigenspaces. Published form: `Sigma = diag(5,...,5,3,...,3,1,...,1)` and `Sigma-hat` with entries `5,...,5,2,...,2,(2+eps),...,(2+eps)`, the block of interest being the MIDDLE d eigenvectors, so the population gap `min(5-3,3-1) = 2` is two-sided. Both force `||V-hat O - V||_F = sqrt(2d)` for every O and match the aligned-basis constant up to `(1+eps)`.
items.notes:
Preprint construction formalized 2026-08-04 in `YuWangSamworth2015/YuWangSamworth2015/Symmetric/OrthogonalSharpness.lean`; the PUBLISHED middle-block construction formalized 2026-08-13 in `YuWangSamworth2015/YuWangSamworth2015/Symmetric/MiddleBlockSharpness.lean`, closing what this census recorded as gap `published-sharpness-example`.

`compiled_generalized` rather than `compiled_exact`: both models are stated for an arbitrary orthonormal basis of an arbitrary finite-dimensional RCLike inner product space, which specializes to the paper's real `p x p` matrices at `EuclideanSpace R (Fin p)`. Each example is checked against the theorems' own hypotheses -- `correspondingEigenblock_*` supplies the branch-selection datum and `internalGap_*` the population gap -- so both are genuine instances of `yuWangSamworth_alignedBasis_le`, not numerical coincidences. Both printed equalities are proved in each model: every aligned orthonormal pair is at distance exactly sqrt(2d), and ||sin Theta||_F = sqrt d, against a bound of sqrt(2d)(1+eps).

The preprint row is what forced the first `CorrespondingEigenblock` CONSTRUCTOR (`correspondingEigenblock_topEigenspace`): the hypothesis had no instance anywhere in the repository, so no concrete pair of covariance operators had ever been checked against it. The published row forced the general one. Its block sits in the MIDDLE of both spectra, so no 'leading d eigenvectors' argument can select it, and the missing foundation was the position of an arbitrary eigenvalue level set inside Mathlib's sorted eigenbasis: `eigenvalues_level_eq_Ico` (every level set is the contiguous index range `[m, m+d)`), `card_filter_lt_eigenvalues_basisDiagonal` (for a diagonal operator, `m` is read off the coefficient list), and `correspondingEigenblock_eigenvalueLevel`, of which the earlier top-eigenspace constructor is now the case `m = 0`.

**Parameter range widened 2026-08-13.** The published middle-block model was formalized for `0 < eps < 1`; the restriction was an artifact of the first proof, not of the construction. What the model actually needs is `2 < 2 + eps < 5`, so that `2 + eps` is the SECOND level of the sorted sample spectrum and the perturbed block occupies the same ordered positions as the population block of threes. Every lemma is now proved for the full range `0 < eps < 3`. `card_middleSharpnessSample_level_three` computes the multiplicity of the level `2 + eps` at `eps = 3` to be `p - d`: it has merged with the leading level `5`, so whenever `2d < p` it differs from the population block's `d` and the two blocks are no longer a corresponding eigenblock; at `eps = 0` the level merges downwards with the `2`s instead. The range is therefore maximal for `2d < p`, which is the case the example is about, and merely sufficient in the degenerate case `p = 2d`, where there is no leading level `5` at all and every `eps > 0` would do. Neither endpoint refutes the sharpness claim -- the construction simply stops describing what it claims to.

`yuWangSamworth_sharpness_middleBlock` now also concludes the achieved distance `sqrt(2d)` for every aligned orthonormal pair, rather than only the arithmetic value of the bound, so its statement carries the sharpness claim its docstring makes.

items.title: Sharpness example: planar rotation, nearby one-dimensional eigenspaces
items.summary: Sigma = diag(3,1) and Sigma-hat = R_eps Sigma R_eps^T give sin Theta = eps against a bound of 2 eps, so the sine bound is tight up to 2 and the vector bound up to 2^{3/2} even at small angles.
items.notes:
Formalized 2026-08-04 in `YuWangSamworth2015/YuWangSamworth2015/Symmetric/PlanarSharpness.lean`. `compiled_generalized`, and the generalization is the interesting part: `Sigma = diag(3,1)` is the operator that is 3 on a line and 1 on its complement -- `TauCeti.twoLevelOperator 1 3 (k * v)` -- and conjugating by a rotation only moves the line. So the pair (Sigma, Sigma-hat) is two two-level models over the same levels, `twoLevelOperator_sub` gives Sigma-hat - Sigma = 2 (P_v-hat - P_v) with no matrix entries, and nothing forces the ambient space to be 2-dimensional: every conclusion holds for two lines in any finite-dimensional space, of which the paper's R^2 is the smallest case. The rotation parameter is replaced by the overlap c = <v, v-hat>, with the paper's eps = sqrt(1 - c^2) the sine.

All three displayed quantities are proved: ||sin Theta||_F = eps, ||v-hat - v||^2 = 2 - 2c, and 2||E||_op/(3-1) = 2 eps -- so the sine bound is tight up to *exactly* the factor 2 the paper claims, at every angle. The example is checked against the theorem's own hypotheses (`correspondingEigenblock_planarSharpness`, `internalGap_planarSharpness`).

Source note: the paper prints v-hat = (sqrt(1-eps^2), -eps)^T, which is the leading eigenvector of R_eps^T Sigma R_eps rather than of R_eps Sigma R_eps^T. The sign changes none of the displayed quantities -- all three depend on v-hat only through <v, v-hat> -- so the model fixes the overlap rather than a sign convention. Recorded rather than silently corrected.

items.title: Equation (4) -- the double-angle identity, FALSE AS PRINTED
items.summary: The paper rewrites sin^2(2 theta) in terms of ‖v-hat - v‖^2. The printed right-hand side omits a square on the factor (2 - ‖v-hat - v‖^2).
items.notes: This is the census's one genuine source defect and it is machine-checked in both directions: the corrected identity is proved, and the printed polynomial is refuted by `norm_num` at inner product 3/5. Substituting t = ‖v-hat - v‖^2 = 2 - 2c gives sin^2(2 theta) = (1/4) t (2-t)^2 (4-t), and the printed form has (2-t) to the first power. The distilled tex reproduced the ERRONEOUS printed form at its equation (YWS-3) until 2026-07-29, so the repository asserted the false identity in one artifact while refuting it in another; the tex is now corrected, carries the derivation, and cross-references both Lean theorems.
items.next_action: None. Both artifacts now agree and both directions are machine checked.

items.title: Corollary 1 -- the single-eigenvector case, both displays
items.summary: With Delta_j = min(lambda_{j-1} - lambda_j, lambda_j - lambda_{j+1}) > 0 and arbitrary v, v-hat with Sigma v = lambda_j v and Sigma-hat v-hat = lambda-hat_j v-hat: sin Theta(v-hat, v) <= 2 ||Sigma-hat - Sigma||_op / Delta_j, and moreover if v-hat^T v >= 0 then ||v-hat - v|| <= 2^{3/2} ||Sigma-hat - Sigma||_op / Delta_j.
items.notes:
Both printed displays are now stated, at the printed generality (no sample gap, arbitrary unit eigenvectors), and closed on 2026-08-13.

First display: `yuWangSamworth_eigenvector_frame_sinTheta_le`.

Second display: `yuWangSamworth_eigenvector_real_le` is the literal real statement -- over `R`, under `<v-hat, v> >= 0`, `||v-hat - v|| <= 2^{3/2} ||E||_op / Delta_j`. Previously the only statement was `yuWangSamworth_eigenvector_le`, which produces SOME unit scalar `c` with `||c v-hat - v|| <= ...`; over `R` that scalar is `+-1` and the printed inequality is an elementary consequence, but it was not stated, so the exact corollary surface was absent. It also carried the `CorrespondingEigenblock` scope restriction of `YWS-T2-sinTheta`. `yuWangSamworth_eigenvector_frame_le` is the `RCLike` form, where a phase rather than a sign is the honest generalization.

The published article numbers this Corollary 1; the preprint numbers it Corollary 3, which is what the Lean name `yuWangSamworth_eigenvector_le` predates.

Extended 2026-08-13. The two displays above assume `Delta <= |lambda_j - lambda_k|` for every `k != j`; the source assumes only `Delta_j = min(lambda_{j-1} - lambda_j, lambda_j - lambda_{j+1})`. For a sorted spectrum these are the same condition and `OrderedBlockBoundaryGap.gap_of_singleton` is the implication, so `yuWangSamworth_corollary1_sinTheta_le` and `yuWangSamworth_corollary1_real_le` state the corollary with the printed hypothesis.

`yuWangSamworth_corollary1_scalarSample` is the sample-degeneracy witness, and it is the reason the arbitrary-eigenvector formulation is not a luxury: for `Sigma = diag(1, 0)` and `Sigma-hat = I/2` EVERY unit vector of the plane is an admissible `v-hat_1`, and the corollary bounds the angle for each of them. A statement pinning `v-hat` to a chosen eigenbasis of `Sigma-hat` would cover exactly one of them.  **Paper-facing surface added 2026-08-29.** `corollary1_sinTheta` and `corollary1_alignedVector` are the canonical review declarations, matching what `theorem2_sinTheta` did for Theorem 2: real `Real^p`, the source's names, and the exact `SourcePopulationGap Sigma hSigma j j Delta` rather than a lower bound for the denominator. At r = s = j that predicate is the printed Delta_j = min(lambda_{j-1} - lambda_j, lambda_j - lambda_{j+1}), with p = 1 landing in the full-space branch where both exterior gaps are the source's infinity. The earlier `yuWangSamworth_corollary1_*` statements remain the implementation-oriented forms.

**Status changed from `compiled_exact` to `compiled_corrected` on 2026-08-29, and this was a real disclosure defect.** The standalone printed Corollary 1 does not say that `v` and `v-hat` are unit vectors; it says only that they satisfy the two eigenvector equations. Every Lean statement here has always assumed `||v|| = ||v-hat|| = 1`, correctly, because the paper introduces the corollary as the `d = 1` case of Theorem 2, whose frames have orthonormal columns. But calling the result `compiled_exact` asserted that the printed statement is what is compiled, and it is not: without the normalization the second printed display is FALSE, and `corollary1_printed_unnormalized_counterexample` now refutes it -- with `SigmaHat = Sigma` and `v-hat = 2v`, every printed hypothesis holds, the perturbation is zero, and `||v-hat - v|| = ||v||` exceeds the zero bound. See gap `corollary1-printed-normalization`.

semantic_review.claim: With Delta_j = min(lambda_{j-1} - lambda_j, lambda_j - lambda_{j+1}) > 0 and arbitrary v, v-hat with Sigma v = lambda_j v and Sigma-hat v-hat = lambda-hat_j v-hat: sin Theta(v-hat, v) <= 2 ||Sigma-hat - Sigma||_op / Delta_j, and moreover if v-hat^T v >= 0 then ||v-hat - v|| <= 2^{3/2} ||Sigma-hat - Sigma||_op / Delta_j.

items.title: Section 3 -- audit of how statisticians actually apply Davis--Kahan
items.summary: A diagnosis of existing proof patterns: authors apply a mixed-gap theorem then invoke Weyl to recover a population gap; spectral-clustering variants hide an interval-counting requirement; Theorem 2 removes both steps.
items.notes:
This row is literature comparison and is NOT part of the completion denominator; it is recorded because a census that silently omits a section cannot be read as a coverage claim. What changed on 2026-08-13 is that the DETERMINISTIC MATHEMATICAL CONTENT of its claims is now compiled, so the comparison between the two proof routes is a statement about two proved theorems rather than about prose. The claims about what other authors wrote remain prose and are not formalizable.

Claim 1, the mixed-gap-then-Weyl pattern: `mixedGap_of_populationGap_weyl` is the recovery step -- a population exterior gap `Delta` at the selected index block becomes a mixed gap `Delta - eps` once the perturbation is eps-operator-small -- and it is stated for an arbitrary index embedding, so it is more general than the printed prose. `yuWangSamworth_weylRecovered_le_populationGap_bound` then shows `c/(Delta-eps) <= 2c/Delta` when `2 eps <= Delta`: on the event the Weyl step needs, the two-step route lands exactly on the constant that `yuWangSamworth_sinTheta_frame_le` proves with no event at all. What Theorem 2 removes is the hypothesis, not the constant, which is precisely the paper's claim 3.

That the event is not automatic is witnessed by the paper's own Section 1 data: `section1_weylRecovery_fails` records `Delta - ||E||_op = 10 - 11 < 0`, so the recovery yields nothing there, while `internalGap_section1` shows the population-gap theorems still apply.

Claim 2, the hidden interval-counting requirement: `section1_sample_crosses_into_paperBlock` shows that in that same model the fifth sample eigenvalue has crossed into the interval spanned by the article's population block while its population counterpart has not, so `Sigma-hat` has one more eigenvalue there than `Sigma` and a variant assuming a population gap AND equal interval counts is assuming something this example violates.
items.next_action: None. This row is not a formalization gap and must not be counted as one.

items.title: Theorem 3 -- right singular subspaces, population squared-singular gap
items.summary: For rectangular A, A-hat with D = A-hat - A and Delta_sv = min(sigma_{r-1}^2 - sigma_r^2, sigma_s^2 - sigma_{s+1}^2) > 0, ‖sin Theta(V-hat, V)‖_F <= 2 (2 sigma_1 + ‖D‖_op) min(sqrt d ‖D‖_op, ‖D‖_F) / Delta_sv.
items.notes:
The route is the paper's own: transport to the squared Gram operators, then apply Theorem 2. The coefficient `(2 sigma_1 + ||D||_op)` and the `min` numerator are proved as printed.

**Status changed to `compiled_corrected` on 2026-08-13, twice over.**

(a) SCOPE. `CorrespondingRightSingularBlock` inherits the `CorrespondingEigenblock` restriction of `YWS-T2-sinTheta` and is therefore narrower than the printed hypothesis `A v_j = sigma_j u_j` with `V` merely orthonormal. `yuWangSamworth_rightSingularSubspace_frame_le` is the printed statement: an arbitrary ordered right singular frame on each side.

(b) THE PRINTED CONVENTION IS FALSE. Theorem 3 defines `sigma_{rank(A)+1}^2 = -inf`, which makes the denominator infinite whenever `s = rank(A)` and so asserts a zero angle between subspaces that can be orthogonal. This is refuted by `yuWangSamworth_theorem3_printed_rankBoundary_refutation`; see gap `theorem3-rank-boundary` and row `YWS-T3-rankBoundary`. The Lean gap hypothesis is the intrinsic separation of the sorted spectrum of `A*A`, which counts the zero eigenvalues, so what is proved here is the corrected theorem. Calling it 'exact Theorem 4', as the module header did, was not source-faithful.

**Singular-value notation added 2026-08-13, and the row stays `compiled_corrected`.** `YuWangSamworth2015/YuWangSamworth2015/Rectangular/SingularBlock.lean` restates the theorem with consecutive singular indices `r, ..., s` and the squared boundary gap `Delta_sv <= min(sigma_{r-1}^2 - sigma_r^2, sigma_s^2 - sigma_{s+1}^2)`, so a reader can compare it to the printed statement term by term. The bridge is `sq_singularValues_eq_eigenvalues_rightGram`, and it is exactly where the correction lives: `LinearMap.singularValues` is zero past the rank by construction, so squared singular values and the sorted spectrum of `A*A` agree at EVERY ambient index, zeros included -- the corrected convention `sigma_{q+1}^2 = -inf` with `sigma_j = 0` for `j` past the rank, not the printed `sigma_{rank(A)+1}^2 = -inf`. `singularBoundaryGap_of_rank_le` makes the difference concrete: when the block ends at or past `rank(A)` the correct lower boundary gap is `sigma_s^2 - 0`, a finite positive number the caller must supply, where the printed convention offered a vacuous one. The singular-value statements use the same `r`, `s`, `r + d = s + 1` variables.

semantic_review.claim: For rectangular A, A-hat with D = A-hat - A and Delta_sv = min(sigma_{r-1}^2 - sigma_r^2, sigma_s^2 - sigma_{s+1}^2) > 0, ‖sin Theta(V-hat, V)‖_F <= 2 (2 sigma_1 + ‖D‖_op) min(sqrt d ‖D‖_op, ‖D‖_F) / Delta_sv.
semantic_review.note: Theorem 3 is grouped across its right, left, aligned-frame, and printed-rank-boundary rows; the rank-boundary row is a machine-checked refutation of the printed convention rather than a silent repair.

items.title: Theorem 3 -- the identical statement for left singular subspaces
items.summary: The paper states that the identical bounds hold for the corresponding left singular-vector blocks U, U-hat.
items.notes:
Proved as its own statement rather than by an adjoint-symmetry argument from the right-hand case, so the two are independently checkable. Both corrections recorded on `YWS-T3-right` apply verbatim, with the ambient dimension on the left being the codomain dimension: the corrected convention is `sigma_{p+1}^2 = -inf`, not `sigma_{rank(A)+1}^2 = -inf`.

**Singular-value notation added 2026-08-13, and the row stays `compiled_corrected`.** `YuWangSamworth2015/YuWangSamworth2015/Rectangular/SingularBlock.lean` restates the theorem with consecutive singular indices `r, ..., s` and the squared boundary gap `Delta_sv <= min(sigma_{r-1}^2 - sigma_r^2, sigma_s^2 - sigma_{s+1}^2)`, so a reader can compare it to the printed statement term by term. The bridge is `sq_singularValues_eq_eigenvalues_rightGram`, and it is exactly where the correction lives: `LinearMap.singularValues` is zero past the rank by construction, so squared singular values and the sorted spectrum of `A*A` agree at EVERY ambient index, zeros included -- the corrected convention `sigma_{q+1}^2 = -inf` with `sigma_j = 0` for `j` past the rank, not the printed `sigma_{rank(A)+1}^2 = -inf`. `singularBoundaryGap_of_rank_le` makes the difference concrete: when the block ends at or past `rank(A)` the correct lower boundary gap is `sigma_s^2 - 0`, a finite positive number the caller must supply, where the printed convention offered a vacuous one. The singular-value statements use the same `r`, `s`, `r + d = s + 1` variables.

items.summary: Some O-hat in O(d) satisfies ‖V-hat O-hat - V‖_F <= 2^{3/2} (2 sigma_1 + ‖D‖_op) min(sqrt d ‖D‖_op, ‖D‖_F) / Delta_sv, and likewise on the left.
items.notes:
Factored through a single generic Gram transport result so that no perturbation argument is duplicated between the symmetric and rectangular cases; that transport result is `private`, which is the right call for an internal factoring step. The frame-generality and rank-boundary corrections recorded on `YWS-T3-right` apply here too.

**Singular-value notation added 2026-08-13, and the row stays `compiled_corrected`.** `YuWangSamworth2015/YuWangSamworth2015/Rectangular/SingularBlock.lean` restates the theorem with consecutive singular indices `r, ..., s` and the squared boundary gap `Delta_sv <= min(sigma_{r-1}^2 - sigma_r^2, sigma_s^2 - sigma_{s+1}^2)`, so a reader can compare it to the printed statement term by term. The bridge is `sq_singularValues_eq_eigenvalues_rightGram`, and it is exactly where the correction lives: `LinearMap.singularValues` is zero past the rank by construction, so squared singular values and the sorted spectrum of `A*A` agree at EVERY ambient index, zeros included -- the corrected convention `sigma_{q+1}^2 = -inf` with `sigma_j = 0` for `j` past the rank, not the printed `sigma_{rank(A)+1}^2 = -inf`. `singularBoundaryGap_of_rank_le` makes the difference concrete: when the block ends at or past `rank(A)` the correct lower boundary gap is `sigma_s^2 - 0`, a finite positive number the caller must supply, where the printed convention offered a vacuous one. The singular-value statements use the same `r`, `s`, `r + d = s + 1` variables.  **Printed shape closed 2026-08-29.** Until then the only statements carrying this row concluded that SOME pair of orthonormal frames spanning the two blocks achieves the bound. That is the basis-free content and it proves the numerical claim, but the paper rotates V-hat by an orthogonal O-hat and compares against THE SUPPLIED V. This is the same defect found and closed for Theorem 2 on 2026-08-13, when the alignedBasis statements were superseded by alignedFrame; the correction had never been propagated to Theorem 3, and no declaration for singular blocks produced an element of the orthogonal group. `yuWangSamworth_rightSingularAlignedFrame_block_le` and its left twin now conclude the printed shape. The alignment half was factored out first as `exists_unitary_sqrt_sum_sq_norm_frameComp_sub_le` and its real matrix form `exists_orthogonal_sqrt_sum_sq_norm_sub_le`, which take two orthonormal frames and ANY Frobenius sine bound, so no perturbation argument is repeated between the symmetric and rectangular cases. items.title: Theorem 3's convention sigma_{rank(A)+1}^2 = -infinity, FALSE AS PRINTED
items.summary: Theorem 3 defines sigma_0^2 = infinity and sigma_{rank(A)+1}^2 = -infinity. The second convention makes the denominator infinite when s = rank(A), so the printed bound asserts that the sample and population right singular subspaces coincide -- and they can be orthogonal.
items.notes:
Found 2026-08-13; no erratum located. The counterexample is two rank-one orthogonal projections on a real inner product space, instantiated on `R^2` as the projections onto the two coordinate axes: both have rank one, so `r = s = 1 = rank(A)` is admissible and the printed hypothesis holds under the printed conventions, yet the two right singular subspaces are orthogonal and `||sin Theta||_F = 1`. Lean has no `inf` here, so the printed denominator is encoded as 'larger than every real': the refuted claim is that the bound holds for EVERY positive `Delta`.

The repair needs no new theorem. The correct convention is the ambient one the paper's own proof uses -- `sigma_{q+1}^2 = -inf` for right blocks and `sigma_{p+1}^2 = -inf` for left blocks, with `sigma_j = 0` for `min(p,q) < j` -- and the repository's gap hypothesis has always been the intrinsic separation of the spectrum of `A*A`, which counts the zero eigenvalues correctly. This row is the second machine-checked source defect in this paper, alongside `YWS-EQ4-double-angle`.

Strengthened 2026-08-13: the refutation now also concludes `||sin Theta||_F = 1` for the two right singular subspaces, so the statement itself exhibits that they differ nontrivially instead of leaving that to the proof. The corrected reading it points to is now stated in singular-value notation by `singularBoundaryGap_of_rank_le`.

items.title: Rank-one singular-vector corollaries (beyond the printed paper)
items.summary: Direct right and left single-singular-vector bounds, obtained by reusing the symmetric rank-one theorem on Gram operators.
items.notes: The paper does not print these; the lane adds them because the rectangular rank-one case is what applications actually use. Recorded so that the census is not read as claiming they are source items.

items.title: Appendix equations (A7)-(A8) -- the Gram transport identities
items.summary: The identities converting a rectangular perturbation bound into a symmetric one on A^T A and A A^T, producing the (2 sigma_1 + ||D||_op) coefficient. Printed as (A7) and (A8) in the published appendix; (10)-(12) is the preprint numbering.
items.notes: Proved for both the Frobenius and operator branches separately, which is what makes the min in Theorem 4's numerator legitimate rather than a bound on one branch quoted for both.

items.title: The self-adjoint dilation route is a modern alternative, not the paper's
items.summary: The repository additionally proves the singular-subspace bound through the Hermitian dilation [[0, A*],[A, 0]] rather than through squared Gram matrices.
items.notes: Mathematically equivalent to the paper's route and recorded here explicitly so that nobody attributes it to Yu, Wang and Samworth. The distilled tex's transcription audit makes the same point.
items.next_action: None. Keep the attribution note attached to these declarations.

items.title: Lemma A1, inequality half -- orthonormal compression cannot increase the Frobenius norm
items.summary: If U and W have orthonormal columns then ‖U^T M W‖_F <= ‖M‖_F.
items.notes: Restated as a two-sided ideal estimate for the rectangular Frobenius norm rather than copied as a matrix-only helper, with bundled linear-isometry wrappers exposing the paper's orthonormal-column hypothesis directly. `sum_sq_norm_apply_orthonormal_le` (added 2026-08-13, in `ForTauCeti`) is the column-sum form the Theorem 2 proof actually consumes: `sum_i ||M w_i||^2 <= ||M||_F^2` for an orthonormal family `w`. The published article numbers this Lemma A1; the preprint numbers it Lemma 5, which is what the Lean names predate.

items.title: Lemma A1, equality half -- orthonormal rows give equality
items.summary: If instead U and W have orthonormal rows then ‖U^T M W‖_F = ‖M‖_F.
items.notes: The equality half is the direction the appendix proof actually consumes; the inequality half is the one usually quoted. Both are proved. The row-side norm-preservation step `rectangularFrobenius_comp_adjoint_linearIsometry` is `private`; both public forms are listed.
